prize_parts.citation: For an oeuvre that renews poetry, the essay and the book as object through an inventive, grief-driven dialogue with antiquity.

statement.case_for: After reading the colleagues' openings, I keep Carson first. On the common criteria her voice is the most unmistakable on the shortlist. Autobiography of Red recasts a Stesichorean fragment as a verse novel, and Nox turns elegy into a material object. The invention is tied to real intellectual depth and to grief and desire, so it is more than formal play. The work has been sustained over several decades across poetry, essay, drama and translation, and it has influenced English-language writing. The case rests on this body of work and not on one title. The prize is for a whole authorship, and her hybrid practice is a single, recognizable project. It is not a scatter of unrelated modes. I rely on public knowledge of the major works and have not independently re-read or verified the corpus.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the one Mattson and Olsson raise. The range of modes makes it harder to name one central achievement. Part of the corpus (translations and versions of ancient texts) is derivative by nature, and some works depend on physical book design that a text-only reading loses. Her allusive, classical method may also address a narrower readership than the prize ideally serves. Cărtărescu's single coherent inner cosmos is a more unified achievement, and Michon's compression is more rigorous. Against Carson's endurance there is also the open question whether the late work matches the early peaks.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first for a voice hard to confuse with any other and a coherent inner cosmos. She places Carson third. She finds Carson's range of modes makes a single central achievement hard to define, says the translations and versions must be separated from the original work, and says the endurance of the formal experiments is not yet settled.
responses.response: I accept the separation. The citation should rest on the original verse novel, elegy and essay and treat the classical translations as supporting evidence. On that footing the central achievement can be named: the remaking of the book-length lyric and essay through confrontation with antiquity and loss. I agree that Cărtărescu's project is the more unified, and that is the real competing consideration. I weigh Carson's decades of sustained invention and emotional force somewhat higher. Whether her experiments will endure cannot be settled now. The question before us is sustained quality, and the span of her work supports that. I regard this as a difference of weighting that I cannot fully resolve.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Cărtărescu first and Carson second. He credits Carson's formal achievement and the sustained classical line, but he asks how genre-crossing work fits the will's wording on the idealistic direction and how the translation and scholarship component can be separated from original creation.
responses.response: I take the will's wording seriously but read it as a question about the work's orientation, not its genre. In Nox and Autobiography of Red the formal invention serves an elegiac and erotic seriousness, and that bears on the criterion. I agree the committee has to state this explicitly in the citation and not assume it. On separating the translation component, I share your concern and have addressed it above. I also share your view that the Cărtărescu case is very strong. Where we differ, I think, is mainly on how much weight to put on unity of project against breadth of formal reinvention.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Carson first. She notes that the translations sit at the edge of what counts as original literary work under Nobel's will. She also notes that a text-only reading may miss book design and performance, and that the uneven reception of later hybrid work makes surveying the oeuvre harder.
responses.response: I agree with the translation point and with the limit of text-only reading. I would add that the citation scope should avoid claiming the object-like or performative dimension as the main achievement. I would anchor it in the written text, with Nox's physical form as an extension and not a substitute. This keeps the citation within what the committee can assess from the printed work. I also share your caution that I cannot judge the unevenness of the recent output.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Carson first. He notes that her scholarly and classical allusiveness may narrow the readership the Academy considers essential, that the most radical books are demanding, and that the case must rest on a body of work. He ranks Cărtărescu second and warns that its very large works risk excess or repetition.
responses.response: I agree that the case has to rest on a body of work and not on one title, and that the allusive method narrows access. I would qualify the readership point. Her grief-driven books, Nox above all, reach readers without specialist classical training. That is a judgment from public knowledge and not a verified claim about reception. Your reservation about excess in Cărtărescu's longest novels is fair and a counterweight I also hold, because I cannot judge repetition across those works without close reading in Romanian.

uncertainties: How much of Carson's achievement lies in original creation and how much in translation, scholarship and reworking of ancient texts, and how to word the citation so that it rests on the original work.
Whether the hybrid and object-dependent works are fully assessable from the printed text, and whether late work sustains the level of the major books.
Translation coverage for Cărtărescu (especially the poetry and the density of the Romanian prose) and for Michon's compressed French, so comparison with Carson, who writes in English, is asymmetric.

How to weigh unity of a single metaphysical project (Cărtărescu) against breadth of formal reinvention (Carson). Opening support counts are not evidence of literary merit and I do not treat them as such.
I rely on public knowledge of the major works and have not independently read or verified the corpus.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile records collegial service with the other committee members, including election in the same 2019 renewal round as Ellen Mattson, but no connection to any shortlisted writer. My own literary practice is not treated as evidence of preference.
